statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 14% (low), Stress 37% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high).
recommendation: Tail stays below the block threshold through the overnight block. A narrow evidence-based danger window is mapped to 13:30-15:00 UTC on 23 September, covering the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMI release and the EIA crude inventory report, where the forecast reaches the WATCH band. The 18:00-19:00 UTC power hour is projected to touch WATCH a second time.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds its record in an orderly overnight coil; Tail low, Stress moderate on elevated yields and an unresolved Iran file
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 22 September at a record 30,732.40, up 0.82%, but the session's internals were divergent: the S&P 500 finished flat and the Dow fell 0.36% while AI and semiconductor leadership carried the index. The cash path was orderly - the close sat about 38 points below the session high inside a 274-point range - and VIX fell 4.44% to 14.21, so there is no observed evidence of persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or failed retracements. Globex is quiet: NQ trades 31,047.75, up 0.06%, inside a 62-point range on 5.96k contracts. Cross-asset signals conflict rather than align. Crude fell sharply on reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, with WTI near $89.6 and Brent near $98.5, which is equity-supportive, while the 2-year at 4.76% and the 10-year at 4.96% on the latest Federal Reserve H.15 release remain a valuation constraint on long-duration technology. Latest-session breadth is split: semiconductors were uniformly bid, but megacaps closed four up and four down and Communication Services lagged. Asian trading on 22 September erased its early tech-driven gains, which is mean-reverting rather than trending behaviour. Tail is therefore held in the low band at 14%. Stress stays moderate at 37% because the index is extended at a record on narrow leadership, yields are high, and the Iran offer is publicly disputed and unresolved. Conditional risk concentrates in the 13:00-15:00 UTC block on 23 September, where the US cash open, the S&P Global flash PMIs and the EIA inventory report cluster.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. The overnight and European block held a steady low-Tail, normal-mode regime with Tail between 11% and 13%. Tail stepped up around the 22 September US cash open, peaking at 21% in the 14:00 UTC hour as trend-up structure appeared, eased back to 14-17% through midday in mixed mode, returned to 20-21% across the 18:00-19:00 UTC block, then decayed to 15-16% into and after the cash close as the advance stayed orderly.
outlookSummary: The overnight block is scored in the low Tail band: no scheduled US macro, thin Asian liquidity, a 62-point Globex coil and a VIX near 14 support continued two-way conditions, with Iran and UN General Assembly headlines as the main gap channel. Conditional risk builds through the European morning and peaks across the 13:00-14:00 UTC block, where the US cash open, the September flash PMIs and the EIA inventory report cluster and the mapped state reaches WATCH. Risk is projected to decay through the New York afternoon provided the opening move retraces, with the 5-year auction and a Fed speaker as secondary checkpoints, a second WATCH touch in the power hour, and a return to the low band across the CME maintenance break.
